elements.quote: This paper compares the postoperative recovery of patients with acute appendicitis (AA) after laparoscopic appendectomy (LA) and open appendectomy (OA), aiming to determine the optimal diagnosis and treatment plan for appendectomy.
elements.reason: The abstract describes the study as a paper comparing interventions and the title/abstract identify it as a meta-analysis, indicating it is a systematic review/meta-analysis.

elements.quote: This paper compares the postoperative recovery of patients with acute appendicitis (AA) after laparoscopic appendectomy (LA) and open appendectomy (OA), aiming to determine the optimal diagnosis and treatment plan for appendectomy.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly states the main objective: to compare postoperative recovery after LA versus OA to determine the optimal treatment.
The abstract does not report the main inclusion or exclusion criteria (e.g., study designs, participant criteria, outcomes) even though these appear elsewhere in the paper.

elements.quote: Related literature was retrieved from PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, CNKI and Wanfang databases. Articles on LA and OA for AA published between 2010 and 2021 were selected to extract data.
elements.reason: The abstract lists the databases searched and gives the publication date range (2010–2021), indicating information sources and the period searched.
The abstract does not describe any methods used to assess risk of bias in the included studies.

elements.quote: Besides, Stata16.0 was used for meta-analysis.
elements.reason: The abstract states that a meta-analysis was performed using Stata16.0, indicating the method used to synthesize results.

elements.quote: A total of 777 articles were retrieved, and 16 of them were finally selected. Totally, 1251 patients underwent LA, while 898 patients received OA.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the number of retrieved and included studies (16) and the total participants in each group (1251 LA; 898 OA).

elements.quote: LA was associated with lower incidence of adverse reactions [OR = 0.257, 95% CI (0.162, 0.408), P < 0.001], shorter operation time (SMD = - 1.802, 95% CI - 2.435, - 1.169; P < 0.001) and hospitalization (SMD = - 1.184, 95% CI - 1.512, - 0.856; P < 0.001). In addition... less intraoperative blood loss (SMD = - 3.650, 95% CI - 5.088, - 2.212; P < 0.001) and shorter recovery time of gastrointestinal function (SMD = - 3.010, 95% CI - 3.816, - 2.203; P < 0.001). Aside from all these, the counts of leukocyte (SMD = - 0.432, 95% CI: - 0.775, - 0.089; P = 0.013), neutrophil (SMD = - 1.346, 95% CI - 2.560, - 0.133; P = 0.030), and C-reactive protein (SMD = - 2.391, 95% CI - 3.901, - 0.882; P = 0.002) all decreased in a significant manner after LA.
elements.reason: The abstract reports results (effect estimates with confidence intervals and p-values) for the main outcomes of interest.

elements.quote: LA was associated with lower incidence of adverse reactions [OR = 0.257, 95% CI (0.162, 0.408), P < 0.001], shorter operation time (SMD = - 1.802, 95% CI - 2.435, - 1.169; P < 0.001)...
elements.reason: The abstract reports summary estimates (ORs and SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals for meta-analytic results.

elements.quote: LA was associated with lower incidence of adverse reactions... shorter operation time... In addition... LA was found with less intraoperative blood loss... and shorter recovery time of gastrointestinal function...
elements.reason: The abstract compares groups and clearly indicates the direction of effect and that LA is favored for multiple outcomes.
The abstract does not contain any brief summary of limitations of the included evidence (e.g., risk of bias, inconsistency, imprecision).

elements.quote: Conclusion: Compared with OA, LA boasts the advantages of less adverse reactions, shorter operation time and hospitalization, fewer complications, and lower inflammatory response, evidencing its safety and feasibility of applying in the treatment of AA.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation and implication, concluding that LA is safe and feasible and summarizing clinical implications.
The abstract does not report any information about the primary source of funding for the review.
The abstract does not provide a register name or registration number for the review.

elements.quote: Background: This paper compares the postoperative recovery of patients with acute appendicitis (AA) after laparoscopic appendectomy (LA) and open appendectomy (OA), aiming to determine the optimal diagnosis and treatment plan for appendectomy.

elements.quote: Inclusion criteria: (1) Study subjects: AA patients undergoing LA and OA, without age limit; (2) Intervention: LA and OA; (3) Outcome measures: at least any of the followings: incidence of adverse reactions after treatment, postoperative white blood cell count (WBC), postoperative neutrophil count (NEUT), postoperative C-reactive protein (CPR), operation time, intraoperative blood loss; ... recovery time of gastrointestinal function, hospitalization duration; (4)Study design: randomized controlled trials (RCTs) or case-control studies.
elements.reason: For an intervention review, the planned comparisons are defined: population (AA patients), intervention and comparator (LA and OA), and specific outcomes are listed, which satisfies PICO-style reporting of planned comparisons.

elements.quote: Inclusion criteria: (1) Study subjects: AA patients undergoing LA and OA, without age limit; (2) Intervention: LA and OA; (3) Outcome measures: at least any of the followings: incidence of adverse reactions after treatment, postoperative white blood cell count (WBC), postoperative neutrophil count (NEUT), postoperative C-reactive protein (CPR), operation time, intraoperative blood loss; (CIs) for dichotomous and continuous outcomes. ... elements.quote: Since there was significant heterogeneity in the included studies, we conducted sensitivity analyses. The pooled effect size was re-analyzed after removing the included studies one by one, but the new combined results did not change much from the previous ones, suggesting low sensitivity and stability and credibility of the meta-analysis results (Fig. 7A-C).
elements.reason: The authors report performing sensitivity analyses (leave-one-out) and heterogeneity testing (I2) and using random-effects models when I2>50% (text_10), which are methods related to assessing heterogeneity and robustness; however they do not describe methods specifically aimed at exploring causes of heterogeneity (e.g., subgroup analysis or meta-regression).
